title: Big Ten makes decision on scheduling Texas Tech amid gambling fallout - AOL
snippet: The Big Ten Conference has made a decision on whether or not it will allow teams to schedule with Texas Tech after the gambling fallout.
extractedText: Big Ten makes decision on scheduling Texas Tech amid gambling falloutZachary Neel, Red Raiders WireThu, June 11, 2026 at 7:45 PM UTC0Big Ten makes decision on scheduling Texas Tech amid gambling falloutIn the wake of the Brendan Sorsby injunction granted earlier this week and the fallout that has followed, there have been talks among certain athletic directors and conferences about the possibility of boycotting the Texas Tech Red Raiders going forward.The general thought has been that if Texas Tech allows Sorsby to play, despite his admission of rule-breaking through illegal gambling on his own team, then teams would refuse to take the field against the Red Raiders and potentially push the College Football Playoff to ban them from postseason competition.It turns out that might have been a lot of talk, at least at the conference level.AdvertisementOn Thursday, the Big Ten said it will not prohibit teams from scheduling Texas Tech in the future, but will instead leave it up to the teams themselves, according to The Athletic's Ralph D. Russo."The Big Ten is not expected to implement a mandate that would prohibit schools from scheduling Texas Tech, two people involved in the discussions told The Athletic on Thursday," Russo writes. "The Big Ten plans to continue to let schools handle those decisions on their own, the two people said."Of course, this does not mean we won't see teams take matters into their own hands and avoid playing the Red Raiders for moral reasons in the future, but at this point, the conference will not be a unified front.This article originally appeared on Red Raiders Wire: Texas Tech vs. Big Ten? Conference makes decision on scheduling future
author: Zachary Neel, Red Raiders Wire
